title: Library Imports
content: Imports Mathlib's `SimpleGraph` for graph structure, `Connectivity.Subgraph` for reachability and distance, `Nat.Basic` and `Finset.Card` for counting edges in finite graphs.
mathContext: Mathlib's `SimpleGraph V` provides symmetric irreflexive adjacency on vertex type $V$. The `edgeFinset` gives the edge set as a `Finset` when $V$ is finite, enabling edge counting.

title: Graph Distance
content: Shortest path length between vertices $u$ and $v$ in graph $G$. Returns $\infty$ if the vertices are not connected, otherwise the standard graph distance $d_G(u,v)$.
mathContext: Graph distance $d_G(u,v) = \min\{|P| : P \text{ is a } u\text{-}v \text{ path}\}$ is a metric on connected components. The use of $\mathbb{N}_{\infty}$ (extended naturals) handles disconnected pairs cleanly.

title: Graph Diameter
content: The diameter of $G$, defined as $\sup_{u,v} d_G(u,v)$. For connected finite graphs this equals $\max_{u,v} d_G(u,v)$, the longest shortest path.
mathContext: The diameter $\mathrm{diam}(G) = \max_{u,v \in V} d_G(u,v)$ measures the 'worst case' distance. Diameter 2 means every pair of vertices has a common neighbor.

title: HasDiameter Predicate
content: Graph $G$ has diameter exactly $d$: (1) $G$ is connected, (2) all distances $\le d$, and (3) some pair achieves distance exactly $d$. The three-part definition ensures the diameter is precisely $d$.
mathContext: The three conditions formalize $\mathrm{diam}(G) = d$: connectivity ensures all distances are finite, the upper bound gives $\mathrm{diam}(G) \le d$, and the witness gives $\mathrm{diam}(G) \ge d$.

title: HasDiameter2
content: Specialization: $G$ has diameter exactly 2. Equivalently, $G$ is connected, non-complete, and every two non-adjacent vertices have a common neighbor.
mathContext: Diameter 2 graphs are characterized by the common neighbor property: $\forall u,v$, either $uv \in E$ or $\exists w,\; uw, wv \in E$. The complete graph has diameter 1, so diameter 2 requires at least one non-edge.

title: Edge Deletion
content: Removes edge $\{u,v\}$ from $G$: adjacency $x \sim y$ holds in the new graph iff $x \sim_G y$ and $\{x,y\} \ne \{u,v\}$. Preserves symmetry (via `Set.pair_comm`) and irreflexivity.
mathContext: Edge deletion is the fundamental operation for studying critical edges. The resulting graph $G - uv$ has $|E(G)| - 1$ edges and may increase the diameter if $uv$ was a 'bridge' for some shortest path.

title: Critical Edge
content: Edge $uv$ is critical if $uv \in E(G)$ and deleting it destroys the diameter-2 property: $\mathrm{diam}(G - uv) > 2$ (or $G - uv$ is disconnected).
mathContext: An edge $uv$ is critical for diameter 2 iff there exist vertices $x, y$ whose unique shortest path of length $\le 2$ uses $uv$. Equivalently, after deletion, some pair loses all common neighbors and the edge itself.

title: All Edges Critical
content: Every edge in $G$ is critical for diameter 2. This defines the 'minimal' or 'edge-minimal' diameter-2 property: no proper spanning subgraph has diameter 2.
mathContext: A graph with all edges critical is called **diameter-critical** or **minimal**. It is edge-minimal among all spanning subgraphs with diameter 2. Note this is different from being a subgraph-minimal diameter-2 graph (which could have fewer vertices).

title: Minimal Diameter-2 Graph
content: The conjunction: $G$ has diameter 2 AND every edge is critical. This is the central object of Problem #742 — the question is how many edges such a graph can have.
mathContext: The class of minimal diameter-2 graphs is closed under isomorphism but not under taking subgraphs. The extremal question $\max |E(G)|$ subject to $G$ being minimal diameter-2 on $n$ vertices is the content of the Murty-Plesník conjecture.

title: Edge Count
content: The number of edges $|E(G)| = |\text{edgeFinset}(G)|$, using Mathlib's `edgeFinset` which gives the set of unordered pairs $\{u,v\}$ with $u \sim v$.
mathContext: For a simple graph on $n$ vertices, $0 \le |E(G)| \le \binom{n}{2}$. The Murty-Plesník bound $n^2/4$ is approximately half of the Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(n, K_3) = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$, which is not coincidental — the extremal graph $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$ is the same.

title: Murty-Plesník Bound
content: The conjectured upper bound $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ on edges in a minimal diameter-2 graph. This equals the number of edges in the balanced complete bipartite graph $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$.
mathContext: The bound $n^2/4$ appears throughout extremal graph theory: it is also the Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(n, K_3)$ (Mantel 1907) and the maximum edges in a bipartite graph on $n$ vertices. The coincidence with the Turán number reflects the fact that the extremal graph is bipartite and triangle-free.

title: Complete Bipartite Has Diameter 2
content: The complete bipartite graph $K_{a,b}$ (with $a,b \ge 1$) has diameter 2 and exactly $a \cdot b$ edges. Any two vertices in the same part are connected via a vertex in the other part.
mathContext: $K_{a,b}$ has vertex set $A \sqcup B$ with $|A|=a$, $|B|=b$, and edges between all cross-part pairs. Diameter is 2 since same-part vertices are at distance 2 (via any vertex in the other part). For $a = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$, $b = \lceil n/2 \rceil$, the edge count is $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$.

title: Balanced Bipartite Is Minimal
content: $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$ is a minimal diameter-2 graph: every edge is critical. Deleting any cross-edge disconnects the two endpoints from the 2-step path.
mathContext: In $K_{a,b}$ every edge $uv$ (with $u \in A$, $v \in B$) is critical: after deleting $uv$, the vertices $u$ and $v$ are still at distance 2 (via other vertices), but if $a = 1$ or $b = 1$ then deleting the unique edge between $u$ and $v$ increases the diameter. For balanced bipartite with $a,b \ge 2$, criticality requires a more subtle argument involving the structure of common neighbors.

title: Füredi's Theorem (1992)
content: For sufficiently large $n$, every minimal diameter-2 graph on $n$ vertices has at most $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges. This settles the Murty-Plesník-Ore conjecture.
mathContext: Füredi's proof uses a combination of extremal graph theory techniques. The key insight is that in a minimal diameter-2 graph, the neighborhood structure is highly constrained: for each edge $uv$, there must exist a 'private witness' — vertices whose only path of length $\le 2$ uses $uv$. Counting these witnesses leads to the bound. The 'sufficiently large' threshold $N_0$ is not explicitly determined.

title: Bound Is Tight
content: Proved theorem: for every $n \ge 2$, there exists a minimal diameter-2 graph with exactly $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges. The proof instantiates the balanced complete bipartite graph axiom.
mathContext: The proof is a direct application of `balanced_bipartite_minimal`: for any $n \ge 2$, $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$ witnesses the bound. This shows the Murty-Plesník bound is not just an upper bound but is achieved — the problem is completely resolved.

title: Diameter-Critical Graph (General)
content: A graph is diameter-$d$-critical if it has diameter $d$ and deleting any edge increases the diameter. This generalizes minimal diameter-2 to arbitrary diameter values.
mathContext: For diameter $d \ge 3$, the extremal problem $\max |E(G)|$ over diameter-$d$-critical graphs on $n$ vertices has different answers. The $d = 2$ case is the Murty-Plesník conjecture; for $d \ge 3$, the bounds involve different extremal constructions.

title: Minimal Iff Critical
content: Proved theorem: `IsMinimalDiameter2 G ↔ IsDiameterCritical G 2`. The two definitions coincide for diameter 2, showing our specialized definition is consistent with the general framework.
mathContext: The proof unfolds both definitions and shows they are logically equivalent. The forward direction extracts the diameter and criticality, the backward direction reconstructs the conjunction. This is a sanity check that the specialized and general definitions agree.

title: Main Result: Erdős Problem #742
content: Proved theorem combining both directions: (1) Füredi's bound $|E(G)| \le n^2/4$ for large $n$, and (2) tightness via the balanced complete bipartite graph. The proof is `⟨furedi_theorem, bound_is_tight⟩`.
mathContext: The conjunction packages the complete resolution: the upper bound (from Füredi's axiom) and the matching lower bound (from the proved `bound_is_tight` theorem). This is the standard format for solved extremal problems: optimal bound + extremal construction.
